about-amanda-003.raw: I’m Amanda D’Souza. I have been teaching science for more than 25 years, and my career has taken me through Canada, Japan, Australia, England, Egypt, Barbados, Qatar and Vietnam. I spent about 20 years living and working internationally, teaching students from many different backgrounds and working within very different school systems. That has given me a broad view of education, but it has also shown me something very practical: a student can move from one school or curriculum to another and suddenly appear to have “gaps” simply because the sequence, terminology or expectations have changed. I understand how important it is to find those gaps without turning them into a judgement about the student’s ability.

about-amanda-005.raw: Over the years I have taught IB Diploma Biology, Chemistry and Environmental Systems and Societies; IB MYP Science; the International Middle Years Curriculum; GCSE and IGCSE Biology and Chemistry, including Combined and Coordinated Science; AS and A-Level Biology; and Ontario secondary science. I have also led science departments in Vietnam and Barbados and worked in curriculum development, assessment and teacher mentoring. Since 2013, I have worked as an IB Biology Assistant Examiner, with experience assessing HL Paper 2 and Internal Assessments against IB criteria. That work has given me a close understanding of how IB assessment criteria are applied and, importantly, of the difference between knowing the science and communicating that knowledge effectively under assessment conditions.

about-amanda-008.raw: My own academic background is in Biology. I completed my Bachelor of Science in Biology at the University of Western Ontario in London, Ontario, in 2000. I then moved to Australia for teacher training, completing a Diploma of Education at the University of Wollongong in New South Wales in 2002. I am an Ontario Certified Teacher (OCT #496538), hold Qualified Teacher Status in England, and have completed Guidance and Career Education Additional Qualification Parts 1 and 2.

about-amanda-010.raw: Those qualifications and years of experience matter, but they are not the whole of good tutoring. For me, the starting point is still the student sitting in front of me. I want students to be comfortable saying when they do not understand something, because there is no value in nodding along to an explanation that has not landed. I use conversation, questions and carefully chosen tasks to see what a student really understands, and I change the pace or approach when the evidence tells me to.

about-amanda-011.raw: I believe students can be challenged and supported at the same time. I will be honest about what needs work, help turn a large goal into manageable next steps and expect the student to take an active part in the process. Ultimately, I want students to understand more and trust themselves more — to become increasingly able to work things out without waiting for someone else to tell them what to do.

about-auxesis-003.raw: Auxesis Education grew from a simple idea: tutoring should help a student become more capable, not more dependent. I want students to understand the science they are studying, but I also want them to become better at learning it. That means learning how to question an idea, make connections, recognise a gap, choose a useful strategy and work out what to do when the answer is not immediately obvious.

about-auxesis-008.raw: What that looks like in practice
about-auxesis-008.text: What that looks like in practice

about-auxesis-009.raw: I do not assume that a grade or label tells me what a student needs. A student can be struggling because of a missing foundation, a misconception, weak study strategies, lack of confidence, difficulty applying what they know, or some combination of those things. I ask questions, watch how the student approaches a problem and test what they really understand. If an explanation is not working, I change the explanation — not the expectation that they can learn it.

about-auxesis-010.raw: I also do not take “that makes sense” as the end point. It is a good start, but understanding has to survive when the example changes. Can the student explain the idea in their own words? Can they recognise when it applies? Can they use it in an unfamiliar situation? That is where we begin to see whether the learning belongs to the student rather than to the explanation they have just heard.

about-auxesis-014.raw: High expectations and strong support belong together. Students need to be able to say, “I don’t understand,” without feeling embarrassed, and they deserve honest feedback about what needs work. Mistakes are useful because they show us where to look next. Sometimes I will break a problem into smaller steps or give a prompt or keyword; at other times I will deliberately step back and give the student more time to work through it independently. The amount of support should change as the learner changes.

about-auxesis-016.raw: I guide the learning, parents provide support and structure, and the student remains actively responsible for their learning. That balance matters. Independence does not mean never asking for help; it means recognising when help is useful, using it well and gradually becoming more able to make decisions for yourself.

faq-017.raw: Regular tutoring is billed in monthly blocks. Payment for the next block is due two days before its first session, and new students pay their first block before tutoring begins. Payment can be made by PayPal or bank transfer. A session can be cancelled without charge with at least 7 days’ notice. With at least 12 hours’ notice but less than 7 days, it can be rescheduled within four weeks, subject to availability. Cancellations with less than 12 hours’ notice and no-shows are charged and cannot be made up.

tutoring-policies-005.raw: Regular tutoring is billed in monthly blocks. Payment for the next block is due two days before its first scheduled session, and new students pay for their first block before tutoring begins. If a session is rescheduled, the dates of future invoices do not move with it. Your rate, currency and any separately charged marking or feedback will always be confirmed in advance. Payment can be made by PayPal or bank transfer.

tutoring-policies-007.raw: If you give at least 7 days’ notice, a session can be cancelled without charge. With at least 12 hours’ notice but less than 7 days, the session can be rescheduled instead. The replacement session must take place within four weeks of the original date, at a mutually convenient time and subject to availability. If it is not used within those four weeks, it expires. Cancellations with less than 12 hours’ notice are charged and cannot be made up. The same applies to no-shows.

tutoring-policies-009.raw: Our role is to guide the student’s thinking without taking over assessed work. We help students understand the task, examine their reasoning and identify areas for further attention, while decisions, analysis and final submitted work remain the student’s own. The work must meet the academic-integrity requirements of their school or examination board.

tutoring-policies-011.raw: Tutoring works best when the student is actively involved. I expect students to attempt tasks, answer and ask questions, and tell me when they need help. Parents can support the process with encouragement and practical organisation, while the student remains actively responsible for their learning. I can provide additional practice when it is useful, but tutoring does not replace school or independent study. While specific achievement cannot be guaranteed, I provide honest feedback about the student’s current understanding, the progress they are making and the most useful next steps.
